docSummary: This is a sizing request for Agency X's eServices AMS estate (12 eServices, one 'Booklet' being decommissioned), using FY25 data (Apr 2025-Mar 2026, a stated 12-month period) converted to monthly figures: SRs 3066/12=255.5, CRs 202/12=16.83, incidents (Sev A+B+C=636)/12=53.0 per month. Severities were mapped Sev A=P1 (24.37%), Sev B=P2 (74.53%), Sev C=P3 (1.10%), P4=0% (no Sev D/P4 category reported). Two automation efforts (account-review tool, log-analysis tool) were discussed separately and are treated as opportunities, not AMS tower work. L1 is run by the agency (out of bidder scope) and an intermediate L1.5 team (3-4 people, 24x7, manual) filters tickets before L2/L3, so pass12 could not be computed and pass23 (L2->L3) is only an approximate '<5%' upper bound. Several figures conflict or look unusual (platform Sev A reported as 6 vs 155, Callup Sev A=140 dominating the total, user counts of <1000 vs 4000 concurrent) and should be verified against source data before use.

towers.label: eServices AMS (12 eServices: Portal, Callup, Manning, Deferment, Payslip, Registration, Clearance, Pay, Awards, Leave and Claims, Retail, Posting)

opportunities.name: Account review automation
opportunities.note: ~12 man-days/month, ~5,000 accounts processed/month, no central database, manual Excel collation with no audit trail; scope updated to 12 sources across 5 categories; short-term plan is a standalone 2-month tool, modular for later AIOps integration.

opportunities.name: Log analysis automation
opportunities.note: Weekly manual log review covering 5 use cases, handled by one person via email/Excel workflow; candidate for automation/AIOps pipeline.

warnings: FY25 SR/CR/incident totals span 12 months (Apr 2025-Mar 2026); figures were divided by 12 to get monthly rates - verify this conversion against source intent.
Conflict: session 3 stated platform-wide Sev A was 6 for FY25, but the session-4 table sums Sev A to 155 - the table value was used; please confirm which is correct.
Callup's Sev A = 140 accounts for ~90% of the total Sev A count (155) - flagged by the bid team itself as a figure to challenge.
Leave and Claims shows 1600 SRs but only 10 CRs, and Retail shows 890 SRs with only 1 CR and 54 job failures - these ratios look unusual and should be checked.
Job Failures (92 total, e.g. Retail 54, Awards 8, Pay 30) are not logged as incidents in the text and were excluded from inc/mix - confirm if they should be tracked separately.
User-count conflict: 'fewer than 1000 users are supported' vs 'Governance: 4000 concurrent users at maximum' - clarify which figure applies.
Booklet eService is mentioned as part of the '12 total' but does not appear as a named row in the FY25 table of 12 - verify whether the table already reflects its removal or is missing a row.
Platform team (18 FTE) and the hosting/cloud environment are run by separate parties (separate tender / separate hosting vendor) and were excluded as towers.
An L1.5 team (3-4 people, 24x7, manual ticket filtering/routing) sits between L1 and L2; its workload is not counted in pass12/pass23 per instructions, only in context here.
pass12 (L1->L2) could not be set because L1 is explicitly out of the bidder's scope (run by the agency's help desk).
pass23 was approximated from 'less than 5% are handled at L3' - treat as an upper bound, not an exact observed rate.
incumbentFTE of 33 is the midpoint of the stated 30-36 person range.
No engagement term/duration was stated anywhere in the notes - eng.term omitted.
No delivery-location information for the bidder's own team was given (hosting is in Singapore via a separate hosting vendor, which is not the same as delivery location) - eng.region/locMix omitted.
Severity data only had three bands (Sev A/B/C); no P4-equivalent category was reported, so mix.P4 was set to 0.
